title: Unit margin bridge and HC probing — march 2026 workbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
A compact workbook-style memo to bridge current per-unit gross margin to target margin through three levers: price (per-token / per-embedding), headcount / ops efficiency (FTEs supporting hosted + dedicated), and throughput mix (model mix & quantization). This is a working sheet for scenario testing ahead of the Mar 12 finance review.

Key assumptions (baseline):
- Baseline ARR contribution window: next 12 months.
- Avg request token length (hosted): 120 input + 160 output = 280 tokens
- Embedding calls: avg 1k tokens equivalent pricing unit (we normalize to 1 embed unit).
- Baseline price mix: 80% hosted (pay-as-you-go), 12% dedicated (committed), 8% private/on-prem.
- Current blended revenue/unit (normalized): $0.012 per token-equivalent.
- Direct cost per token-equivalent (cloud infra + model licensing + networking): $0.0065
- Contribution margin (baseline): 45.8%
- Support/ops overhead allocated per token-equivalent: $0.0025

Quick table: baseline rolling 12m unit bridge (per 1k token-equivalents)
| Item | $/1k tokens | Notes |
|------|------------:|-------|
| Blended revenue | 12.00 | baseline normalized (cents) |
| Direct infra & license cost | -6.50 | GPU runtime, licensing & storage |
| Raw gross margin | 5.50 | 45.8% |
| Allocated ops / SRE / support | -2.50 | per-unit overhead |
| Contribution margin (post-ops) | 3.00 | 25.0% |

Target: move contribution margin from 25% to 35% across the next 12 months. Actionable lever sizing below.

Levers and discrete scenarios (high-level):
1) Price experiments (hosted): run A/B test on a 10% sample of new signups with 5% price uplift on text generation rates; measure churn and take rate. Modeled elasticity assumptions: price elasticity -0.6 for small customers, -1.2 for price-sensitive low-commit customers.
2) HC anchoring and productivity: hire plan ties to throughput bands. Two productivity interventions: automation of tiered support (reduces ops allocation by 30% per FTE) and centralization of model ops (reduces infra waste by 8%).
3) Throughput & model-mix: shift 15% of requests to quantized Llama-derivative variant with ~20% lower direct cost and 3–5% quality penalty (monitored via eval sets).

Scenario engine (3 canonical scenarios):
- Conservative: price = 0% change, HC +2 FTEs (net ops cost +$0.4/1k tokens), model mix shift 5% to cheaper models. Margin outcome: 22% contribution.
- Base (most likely): price +3% on hosted, HC flat but productivity improvements (ops allocation -10%), model mix shift 10%. Margin outcome: 29% contribution.
- Aggressive: price +7% phased, HC -1 net (automation offsets), model mix shift 20%, committed contract uptick (dedicated share +5%). Margin outcome: 38% contribution.

Headcount plan snippet (quarterly phasing, FTEs):
| Role cluster | Q2 add | Q3 add | Q4 add | Total EOY delta | Notes |
|--------------|-------:|-------:|-------:|---------------:|-------|
| SRE / Ops | 1 | 0 | 0 | +1 | focus on observability, reduces incident cost |
| Support (tier 2) | 0 | 1 | 0 | +1 | automation roadmap ready to reduce per-ticket time |
| Model Ops | 0 | 0 | -1 | -1 | consolidation of quantized model serving |
| Finance / Pricing Analyst | 0 | 1 | 0 | +1 | run price experiments + dashboards |
| Total | 1 | 2 | -1 | +2 | net +2 FTEs by EOY |

Pricing sensitivity matrix (blended impact on contribution margin):
- Variable inputs: hosted price delta (-5%, 0%, +5%, +10%), elasticities by cohort (enterprise: -0.2, mid-market: -0.6, low-touch: -1.1).
- Output: blended revenue change and margin delta per 1k tokens:
Sample results (rounded):
| Hosted price delta | Blended revenue change % | Contribution margin delta (ppt) |
|--------------------:|------------------------:|-------------------------------:|
| -5% | -3.6% | -3.0 ppt |
| 0% | 0.0% | 0 ppt |
| +5% | +3.4% | +2.8 ppt |
| +10% | +6.6% | +5.2 ppt |

Sensitivity notes: small customers dominate volume but contribute less revenue; price uprates targeted at mid-market & enterprise (tiered routing) give better margin lift with lower churn risk.

Micro-bucket experiment design (for next 6 weeks):
- Bucket A (control): baseline pricing + baseline support SLA.
- Bucket B (price-only): +5% price for mid-market customers, same SLA.
- Bucket C (bundle): +3% price + premium SLA + automatic prefetched KV caching (expected latency improvement).
Metrics to monitor: take-rate, net revenue retention (NRR) by cohort, avg tokens per call, cost per 1k tokens, support ticket volume.

Risk register (top-5):
1) Model quality regression from quantized rollouts -> mitigate with canary on 1% of traffic and continuous eval set.
2) Customer churn in low-touch cohort -> mitigate with targeted discounts and usage-based grace periods.
3) Underestimated infra cost from burst traffic -> mitigate with burst capacity contracts for Dedicated.
4) Slower automation implementation -> rebaseline HC plan if milestones slip 4+ weeks.
5) Measurement gaps (attribution between price vs product changes) -> track feature flags + cohort tagging in analytics.

Short action list before Mar 12 review:
- Finance to finalize macro sensitivity table and attach model (Samir) by Mar 6.
- Product to provide quantization rollout timeline (Lina) by Mar 4.
- Sales to flag enterprise accounts impacted by price changes (Jonah) by Mar 5.
- Build dashboards for micro-bucket A/B within GA + internal BI (Priya) by Mar 9.

Appendix (quick formulas):
- Contribution per 1k tokens = revenue_1k - direct_cost_1k - ops_alloc_1k
- Required price uplift to hit target margin = (target_contribution + direct_cost + ops_alloc - current_revenue) / (volume_weighted_price_sensitivity)

Notes to reviewers: this is a working, intentionally concise workbook — ask for the detailed model (Google Sheets link) if you need the per-customer cohort rows. The goal for Mar 12 is to agree on a 2–3 month experiment slate and an EOY headcount gating rule (if automation milestones achieved, proceed with hiring freeze lift).
